description: SECURITY AUDIT of the whole repository for exposed passwords, secret keys, API tokens, admin credentials, or other committed secrets, and a plain-language written report of findings + remediation saved as SECURITY_AUDIT_FINDINGS.md in the repo root (so it travels in the PR). The repo is PUBLIC and has an admin login, so this is high priority. This feature is largely independent of the code features (read-only scan + one new markdown file) and could run in parallel; it is ordered last only so the report can also note the state after the code fixes. Audience: the founder is NON-TECHNICAL — write in plain, kind, jargon-free language and spell out every acronym on first use.
steps: Scan the entire repository (all tracked files AND full git history) for committed secrets. Cover: passwords, API keys, tokens, admin credentials, private keys, connection strings. Suggested commands: grep across the tree for (password|secret|api[_-]?key|token|admin_key|private[_-]?key|BEGIN PRIVATE KEY|sk-|AKIA|ghp_|xox[baprs]-); and `git log --all -p | grep -inE '(sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|xox[baprs]-)'` to catch anything ever committed then removed.

Correctly classify what is found. VERIFIED-SAFE facts already confirmed during planning that the report should state plainly: (a) all REAL secrets are read from environment variables via os.environ.get (ADMIN_KEY, ADMIN_USER, AHP_UNIFIED_SECRET, ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, DEEPGRAM_API_KEY, DAILY_API_KEY, HUME_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, FREESOUND_API_KEY, NTFY_TOPIC, AHP_DATA_SECRET) and are NOT in the repo; (b) app.secret_key falls back to os.urandom(32) when unset; (c) the .env-looking values and /api/keys credentials in core/axiom_harmony_unified_app.py (around _HONEYTOKEN ~line 11685, the fake DB_PASSWORD/SECRET_KEY/API_KEY/PAYMENT_SECRET ~line 11856, the fake key list ~line 11912) are DELIBERATE HONEYPOTS — fabricated fake secrets planted to catch attackers, not real credentials; the report must make clear these are intentional decoys and safe; (d) admin login uses constant-time comparison (secrets.compare_digest) against ADMIN_KEY with rate-limiting and lockout on failed attempts (_defend/_flag_hostile).

Independently RE-VERIFY those facts during the scan (do not just copy them) and report any NEW finding the planning pass may have missed. If a genuine real secret is found committed anywhere (including history), treat it as a critical finding: document exactly where, and the remediation (rotate the secret immediately, remove from code/history, move to an environment variable).

Note the hardening observations found during planning as recommendations (not necessarily active leaks): (1) session cookies do not set SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE / SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE explicitly — recommend setting SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=True and SAMESITE='Lax' or 'Strict' since the site is HTTPS on Render; (2) the /admin docstring references opening /admin?key=YOUR_ADMIN_KEY — putting a secret in a URL query string risks it landing in server/proxy logs and browser history; recommend the POST login form only and, if any ?key= handling exists, removing it. Verify whether ?key= is actually honored in code and report the true state.

Write SECURITY_AUDIT_FINDINGS.md in the repo root. Structure it plainly: (1) a one-paragraph plain-language summary a non-technical founder can understand ('the good news / what to do'); (2) 'What we checked'; (3) 'What we found' — clearly separating REAL problems (if any) from things that LOOK like secrets but are safe on purpose (the honeypots); (4) 'What to do' — concrete remediation steps written so the founder only ever has to make a decision or click in the Render/GitHub dashboard, never run a command (per CLAUDE.md the founder does no technical steps); (5) a short 'For the technical helper' appendix with exact file/line references. Spell out acronyms on first use (API = Application Programming Interface, etc.). Do NOT reproduce any real secret value in the report; for honeypot values, describe them as fake decoys without presenting them as if usable.
Verify the report file is created and the scan commands were actually run (paste the key scan command outputs into this feature's findings).
acceptance_criteria: SECURITY_AUDIT_FINDINGS.md exists in the repo root.
The report is written in plain, non-technical language, spells out acronyms on first use, and never asks the founder to run commands.
The report clearly distinguishes any real committed secrets (with remediation) from the deliberate honeypot decoys (explained as safe/intentional).
The scan covered both the working tree and full git history; results are recorded in findings.
If any real secret is found, remediation (rotate + remove + move to env var) is spelled out; if none, the report says so plainly and confidently.
Hardening recommendations (session cookie flags; no admin key in URL) are included as recommendations.
findings:
RESULT: NO REAL SECRET FOUND anywhere in the working tree OR the full git history (267 commits). Report written to repo root as SECURITY_AUDIT_FINDINGS.md (plain-language, non-technical audience, acronyms spelled out, never asks founder to run commands, with a 'For the technical helper' appendix). Docs-only change; no code touched, so the verify.sh gate is unaffected.

SCAN OUTPUTS (all run):
(1) test -f SECURITY_AUDIT_FINDINGS.md -> REPORT_EXISTS.
(2) grep -rnE '(sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|xox[baprs]-)' . (excluding this feature file) -> no matches, scan-exit=1.
(3) git log --all -p | grep -inE '(sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36})' -> no matches, exit=1.
(4) grep 'BEGIN .*PRIVATE KEY' tree + history -> only hit is this feature file's own instruction text; none real.
(5) connection-string scan (postgres/mysql/mongodb://user:pass@) -> none.
(6) hardcoded password/secret/api_key/token='literal' scan -> only hits were _HONEYTOKEN decoy references and doc placeholders 'your_key_here'/'your-key-here' in core/zenisys_music_engine.py and download_scenes.py.
(7) No .env / secrets / credential files tracked, on disk, or ever in history.

VERIFIED-SAFE (independently re-confirmed, not just copied):
- (a) All real secrets read via os.environ.get, NOT in repo: ADMIN_KEY, ADMIN_USER, AHP_UNIFIED_SECRET, ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, DEEPGRAM_API_KEY, DAILY_API_KEY, HUME_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, FREESOUND_API_KEY, NTFY_TOPIC, AHP_DATA_SECRET, AHP_PEPPER.
- (b) app.secret_key at line 88 falls back to os.urandom(32).hex() when unset. NOTE: a second assignment (~line 12323) derives it as sha256('innerlight-founder-session::' + ADMIN_KEY) - deterministic from ADMIN_KEY, acceptable; reported in appendix.
- (c) Honeypots CONFIRMED deliberate: _HONEYTOKEN ~line 11808; _fake_env_body() ~11819 (fabricated DB_PASSWORD/SECRET_KEY/API_KEY/PAYMENT_SECRET); decoy routes /.env, /api/keys, /api/v1/keys, /wp-login.php, /wp-admin, /admin.php, /phpmyadmin; replay tripwire _honeytoken_watch() before_request ~12047. All fake, none usable. Reported clearly as intentional safe decoys.
- (d) admin_login() (~12639) uses secrets.compare_digest on username+password with _defend() progressive tarpit/lockout and _flag_hostile('admin-login-fail') on failure.

?key= LOGIN TRUE STATE: The /admin docstring (line 13331) says 'Open /admin?key=YOUR_ADMIN_KEY' but NO code reads request.args.get('key'). Access is gated ONLY by session['founder_ok'] (set by POST /admin/login form) or _has_watch_access(). The query-string login is NOT honored - only the docstring is stale/misleading. Recommended deleting the docstring line.

ENCRYPTION MODULE (core/ahp_encryption.py) HIGH-LEVEL: SOUND. AES-256-GCM AEAD; default KDF now scrypt (N=2^15,r=8,p=1) - stronger than the PBKDF2-390k legacy path which is retained read-only for v1 records; fresh 16B salt + 12B nonce per record; version/context bound as GCM AAD; optional HKDF-mixed AHP_PEPPER server secret. Honest that it is classical (not post-quantum). No rewrite; assessed only.

HARDENING RECOMMENDATIONS (not active leaks): (1) No SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE / SAMESITE / HTTPONLY set anywhere - recommend app.config.update(SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=True, SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=True, SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE='Lax') since Render is HTTPS. (2) .gitignore only lists __pycache__/ and *.pyc - recommend adding .env. (3) Delete the misleading ?key= docstring.

NO ROTATION REQUIRED (no real secret found). If one had been found, remediation (rotate in provider dashboard + remove from code/history + move to env var) would be the founder/orchestrator's job, not this audit's, and the value would NOT be printed.
